text:
incident-bot: Alert: high 5xx percentage observed for Hosted API (eu-west-1) and multiple Dedicated pools in eu-west-1. Threshold triggered: 5xx > 2% for 3m. Alert link: <https://alerts.redwood.internal/alerts/12345|alert-12345> :rotating_light:

ana-sre: acked. I'm oncall. Looking at traces and logs now.

emily-prod: seeing customer-facing errors, quick sample: 
```
2026-03-15T01:02:15Z ERROR auth: decrypt failed for key arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:111222333: key/abcd-... AccessDeniedException
5xx_count: 124 reqs/min
```
This looks like KMS failures during token/model key decrypt.

raj-infra: I can confirm spikes coming from auth token decrypts and model artifact loads in eu-west-1. CloudWatch shows a KMS API error rate spike starting ~01:00 UTC.

lucy-support: customer reports: "requests time out with 503" for hosted endpoints in EU region. A few Dedicated customers also paged. We're triaging customer-impacted list now.

mike-sre: Datadog metrics are delayed (we see ~2-3m ingestion lag) — correlating with the same window. Logs from gateway show repeated 500 responses while waiting on decrypt.

ana-sre: initial mitigation plan: 1) activate regional fallback routing for hosted traffic (route eu-west-1 -> eu-central-1) 2) promote local KV cache for model keys to avoid KMS calls where possible 3) open AWS case for KMS/STS in eu-west-1. Can someone run the routing change?

raj-infra: on it. Running routing change (will be quick):
```
# rollout fallback for hosting
redwoodctl routing update --from-region eu-west-1 --fallback eu-central-1 --priority 70
```
Applying now -> will monitor. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

deploy-bot: Routing change rollout started by raj-infra (id: rc-20260315-01). Canary set to 5% -> increasing to 50% over 2m.

emily-prod: enabling model key local cache for known stable models to reduce decrypts. Patch applied on inference nodes in eu-west-1: 
```
# enable local kms cache
kubectl -n inference set env ds/inference-nodes KMS_CACHE=enabled
```
Fallback to cached keys will prevent new decrypt calls for cached artifacts.

aws-status: AWS Notification: "We are investigating elevated error rates for KMS and STS in eu-west-1. Impacting API calls for KMS/STS" <https://status.aws.amazon.com|aws.status>. Case opened: 9876543210.

lucy-support: customers with dedicated pools: we're sending targeted messages: short note + ETA unknown, mitigation in progress. Two customers requested SLA credits, ticketing created.

mike-sre: after routing started, 5xx rate on hosted dropped from 3.1% -> 0.9% in 7m. Dedicated pools still show some residual failures due to key failures during model loads.

ana-sre: good. Keep the fallback for now and monitor. Raj, can you coordinate with infra to temporarily increase model cache TTLs and block aggressive background model reloads? That should reduce KMS calls.

raj-infra: will increase TTL and throttle reloads: 
```
redwoodctl config set --key model.cache.ttl --value 7200
redwoodctl config set --key model.reload.concurrent --value 1
```
Applying across eu-west-1 nodes.

emily-prod: also enabling a degraded-serving mode for Dedicated pools to serve cached model parameters only (no hot-swapping). This avoids model pulls that trigger KMS decrypt.

ana-sre: AWS has acknowledged KMS instability, engineering: prepare a post-incident runbook item to evaluate resilience: local key caching, longer TTLs, fallback routing automation.

deploy-bot: Canary completed: routing fallback increased to 50% then 100%. Rollout id rc-20260315-01 marked successful.

mike-sre: monitoring: hosted 5xx back to baseline. Dedicated error rate down to ~0.4% but occasional spikes when model reloads happen.

lucy-support: updated customers: message sent to impacted accounts summarizing mitigation and we offered dedicated-fallback contact.

aws-status: Update: "Issue causing increased error rates for KMS/STS in eu-west-1 has been isolated to an internal control plane throttling. Remediation in progress."

ana-sre: ok team, we'll keep fallback routing and caches in place until AWS confirms full recovery. I'm going to escalate to SEV2 and start the incident doc + timeline. Please add short notes to the doc with what you did (commands, timestamps).

emily-prod: adding log snippets and the KMS error samples to the incident doc now.

raj-infra: I opened AWS support case 9876543210 and requested a bridge. AWS asked for request ids and sample request traces (I posted them in the ticket).

mike-sre: handoff: my shift ends in 20m, ana-sre can you take primary until 11:00 UTC? I'll remain available on pager for follow-ups.

ana-sre: taking it. summary: SEV2 ongoing, primary mitigation = regional routing fallback + local KMS caching + throttled reloads. Impact: Hosted API briefly degraded in eu-west-1, Dedicated pools partially affected during model loads. Customers notified. AWS KMS/STS incident opened (9876543210).

lucy-support: tagging postmortem and customer tickets.

ana-sre: handing off to raj-infra for overnight oncall at 02:00 UTC. raj-infra: please ack when you have control of the bridge and monitoring.

raj-infra: ack. I'll keep routing fallback and cache TTL in place and watch for any AWS "resolved" posts before we roll back.

incident-bot: Incident SEV2 created: INC-20260315-42. Handoff recorded: ana-sre -> raj-infra at 02:00 UTC.

(END THREAD)
